summary: The unit (4:16-4:18, the author's question on Rabbi Akiva and the Kabbalists' citations for worship of Ze'ir Anpin) is mostly faithful, with the terms (sefirot, partzufim, Ein Sof, YHVH, Nukva) as ruled. Faults: ריבה / לרבות rendered 'multiplied' instead of the derashic 'include'; ר"א expanded to 'Rabbi Eleazar' against the pilot ruling; added scare quotes and '(the Orchard)'; in 4:17 the Hebrew full stops were followed so that two clauses have no grammar, Ein Sof is made the choicest of the fathers, and 'to it we worship'; in 4:18 אדני read as 'bases' instead of the Name Adonai, the Aramaic heading lost, and Sefer ha-Kavanot misspelt. Five decision questions are raised.

patches.value: And also about Rabbi Akiva, who was the teacher of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, he too was the greatest of the four who entered the Pardes, and reached the place of stones of pure marble, and entered in peace and came out in peace. It is strange why he included the disciples of the wise, who are flesh and blood, and equated their reverence with the reverence of Heaven. And Rabbi also established it in the Mishnah, tractate Avot, chapter 4, in the name of R. A., he should have included the wife of Ze'ir Anpin, who is the LORD our God, according to their words? Or rather he should have included the fathers of Ze'ir Anpin, who are Abba and Imma?
patches.reason: ר"א stays 'R. A.' with a note, because the paragraph does not name him (pilot ruling); 'Rabbi Eleazar' is an expansion the text does not give. ריבה / לרבות is the exegetical term for extending a verse to include something, not 'multiply' (a disciple, a wife or fathers are not 'multiplied'). The single quotes around the LORD our God are added: the Hebrew has none, and the decisions bar scare quotes. '(the Orchard)' is an addition in the English line; the meaning is in the token note.

The gloss carried an added '(the Orchard)'; the literal sense is already in the token note.
Pilot ruling: ר"א is 'Rabbi Eleazar' only where the paragraph names him; otherwise 'R. A.' with a note.

patches.value: ר"א is written without a name, and the paragraph does not say whom it means, so it stays 'R. A.' and is not expanded.
patches.reason: The old note asserted an attribution ('Rabbi Eleazar') the paragraph does not give.

patches.value: ריבה (and לרבות at 4:16.48 and 4:16.62) is the exegetical term for extending a verse to include something it does not name; literally 'increased'. The subject is Rabbi Akiva: ייפלא על ר' עקיבה ... למה ריבה.
patches.reason: The old note said the Hebrew names no subject. It does: the sentence begins 'and also about Rabbi Akiva ...' and the question is why he included. The verb also needed its sense.

Decisions are silent on ריבה / לרבות. Proposed ruling: fixed 'include' (the derashic ribbui), literal 'increase' in a token note; never 'multiply'. 'Multiplied the disciples of the wise' does not say what the Hebrew says.

patches.value: מורא: 'fear' or 'awe'. Rendered 'reverence' here and in למורא שמים. A ruling is needed whether the word is 'fear' (as Deut 6:13 is 'The LORD your God you shall fear', the verse behind this comparison) or 'reverence'.
patches.reason: Decisions render the root ירא as 'fear' in Deut 6:13 but are silent on מורא. Proposed ruling: מורא → 'fear' fixed ('the fear of Heaven'), so that the link to the verse shows in English.

patches.value: ורבי' is written with an apostrophe, so it is an abbreviation, probably of ורבינו ('and our Rabbi'). Read here as the bare title of the Mishnah's redactor, Rabbi Yehudah ha-Nasi. The expansion is not settled.
patches.reason: The decisions require every abbreviation to be expanded but do not cover ורבי'. Proposed ruling: 'and our Rabbi' if the abbreviation is ורבינו (the title of Rabbi Yehudah ha-Nasi), with a note; the owner to confirm.

value: The question is introduced by ייפלא ('it is strange') and למה ('why'). Its subject is Rabbi Akiva, the subject of the long clause before it: ייפלא על ר' עקיבה ... למה ריבה.
קבעה (4:16.38): 'established it', the object is the saying the author has just described, which he does not restate.
The two questions are the author's own. The second is offered as the alternative to the first, with או יותר ('or rather').
The author's Hebrew has no verb of quotation here; the saying is cited as Mishnah, and the question is his.
ריבה and לרבות (4:16.26, 4:16.48, 4:16.62) are the exegetical term for extending a verse to include something it does not name; the English says 'included'.
patches.reason: The first note said the verb has no named subject; it does (Rabbi Akiva). A note on ריבה / לרבות is added.

patches.value: §29. And in Sefer ha-Berit, part 1, Treatise 20, chapter 15, the author of Mishnat Chasidim wrote in the book Yosher Levav: "that the name 'the Holy One, blessed be He', which is customary in our mouths, and that by the name YHVH we call Him, is the partzuf of Ze'ir Anpin, which is the Holy One, blessed be He, whose soul, hidden in him through the agency of the partzufim inside him, is the First Cause itself, and it we worship in his worship. The general result is that the First Cause, which all the Kabbalists call Ein Sof, is He who created everything out of nothing, and He encompasses that whole existent from without, and in its choicest part, and it is the choicest of the fathers, called Ze'ir Anpin, hidden, chamber within chamber, as a soul in the body, and gives it life. Therefore this choicest part, which is Ze'ir Anpin, who rules over all the creatures, directs them, sustains them, and provides for them, and He is our God, and we are His people, for our souls are His portion, and He, He is the One praised in all the praises said in our holy Torah, which He bequeathed to us, and through it He revealed all the hidden things to us." Thus far his words. And further he went on at length with proofs from the Zohar, and from Tikkunei Zohar, that worship is due to Ze'ir Anpin, who is the middle that connects everything. And further he wrote in the name of the Ari in Likkutei Tanakh on the verse "Trust in the LORD forever and ever, for in Yah, the LORD, is an everlasting rock." And these are his words: "It follows that when a person intends toward Ze'ir Anpin alone, it suffices, for there are found Arikh Anpin, Abba and Imma, clothed one within the other, within Ze'ir Anpin." Thus far his words.
patches.reason: (1) The opening 'and' of ובספר is dropped. (2) The Hebrew full stop after בפינו does not end the clause: 'the name HKBH ... and that by the name YHVH we call him' is one compound subject of 'is the partzuf Ze'ir Anpin'; the English left a subject without its sentence. (3) 'To it we worship' is not English; worship is transitive (decisions: 'and Him you shall worship'). (4) The relative המסתתרת: the soul is 'hidden', not 'whose soul is hidden ... is the First Cause'. (5) והוא הבחור שבאבות (4:17.75) goes with ובמובחר שבו: 'its choicest part, and it is the choicest of the fathers, called Ze'ir Anpin, hidden ...'; the next sentence repeats it as 'this choicest part, which is Ze'ir Anpin'. The English made Ein Sof the choicest of the fathers, and Ze'ir Anpin, and gave 'He ... is hidden' two finite verbs; 'choice' and 'that is' were also wrong. 'Fathers' is not a title. (6) כנשמה is 'as a soul', not 'the soul'. (7) 'Treatise' takes a capital with Gate and Branch. (8) 'Intends on' and 'expanded with proofs' are not English for מכוין ל and האריך.

patches.reason: Follows the English changes.
The vav of ובספר is a word of the Hebrew; it was dropped.
ושבשם carries 'that' (ש); the compound subject needs it.
אותו is the one called; 'it' is wrong for the Holy One, blessed be He.
ולה is the object of עובדים; worship is transitive, 'to it we worship' is not English.
והוא refers to the choicest part (מובחר), not to Ein Sof.
אבות is 'fathers'; the capital F is not in the Hebrew.
מבחר is the choicest part of the existent, taken up from ובמובחר שבו; 'this choice' loses that.
והוא here is 'which is', not 'namely'.
האריך בראיות is 'went on at length with proofs'.
בזעיר אנפין after כיוון is 'toward', as 4:18 renders מכוין ל and תכוין ל.

patches.value: אבות: literally 'fathers', also the word for 'the patriarchs'. Here an epithet of Ze'ir Anpin (the choicest of the avot). Kept as 'fathers', the same word as 4:16.63 (אבותיו); the ruling on 'fathers' or 'patriarchs' is open.
patches.reason: Decisions are silent on אבות in the partzuf passages. Proposed ruling: 'fathers' (lower case, literal) wherever the word is the plural of אב, with a note that it is also 'patriarchs'; never a capital F, which turns it into a title.

value: The first quotation runs from כי (4:17.17) to עכ"ל (4:17.126). It is introduced by כתב (4:17.10) and is in Hebrew.
ולה אנו עובדים בעבודתו (4:17.45-48): ולה ('to it') is feminine, because the cause is feminine; בעבודתו ('in his worship') is masculine, for the partzuf.
הכלל העולה כי (4:17.49-51), 'the general result is that', opens the author's summary of the quotation.
The Ari's quotation is introduced by וז"ל (4:17.157), 'and these are his words'. It cites Isa 26:4 (4:17.148-156); ביה (4:17.153) is 'in Yah', the short form of the Name.
אין סוף (4:17.58-59) is a name in the Kabbalists' usage, literally 'without end'; the author's own argument is about whether it is the First Cause.

The Hebrew full stop after בפינו (4:17.21) does not end the clause: 'the name HKBH ... and that by the name YHVH we call him' is one compound subject of הוא פרצוף זעיר אנפין. Likewise והוא (4:17.75) refers back to the choicest part (מובחר), and והוא (4:17.92) takes it up again.
patches.reason: The English followed the stop; the note shows the clause.

patches.value: Also, in the book Etz Chayyim by Rabbi Chayyim Vital, Gate of the Generalities, chapter 11, he wrote that our teacher Moses said to Israel at their entering the land: "But you who cleave to the LORD your God are alive, every one of you, today," for the LORD your God is Ze'ir Anpin and his Nukva, and Israel who entered the land were, etc. See there. Also in Sefer ha-Kavanot, in the customs of the Ari, he wrote that every time you utter the name YHVH, intend toward Ze'ir Anpin, and intend in it thus: Yod-Heh-Vav Ze'ir Anpin, and the last Heh of it is Malkhut (Kingship). Intend that a complete name be made on Adonai, in such a way, etc. See there. Likewise, in the book Machberet ha-Kodesh, in the order of the Musaf of Shabbat, 20, that the hosts of angels above will give a crown to Ze'ir Anpin, who is the LORD our God. See there, folio 40a. Also in Mikdash Melekh, 4, 12, beginning with the words 'the Great God', it is explained that He is called 'the Great God' only in Ze'ir Anpin, and in Chokhmah (Wisdom) He is called wise, etc. And whoever intends toward Ein Sof, because of His exaltedness that He has no name, and no point that would limit Him, his prayer is not a prayer, rather he should intend toward Him while He is clothed in His attributes, etc. And see below, §100, in the name of Nachalat Yosef.
patches.reason: (1) Sefer ha-Kavanot is the conventional title (pilot ruling), and 'the book Sefer' says ספר twice. (2) שם שלם is 'a complete name' (no article); על אדני is the Name Adonai, in a passage on the divine names and Malkhut, not 'the bases'. (3) The words after ד"ה, אלהא רברבא, are the cited heading and were lost from the English; the verb נקרא has no subject in the Hebrew and the next clause (ובחכמה נקרא חכם) is 'He is called wise', so the first must be 'He is called the Great God', not 'the Great God is called'. (4) Stray full stops and lower case after them ('Malkhut (Kingship). intend', 'Ze'ir Anpin. and in Chokhmah') where the Hebrew has a comma or a new sentence.

patches.value: Sefer ha-Kavanot: 'the Book of Intentions'. Kavanot are the intentions of the mind in prayer and in the Name.

patches.value: אדני read as the Name Adonai (the name of Malkhut). The same letters can be read as the plural of אדן, 'bases' or 'sockets'; see apparatus.

patches.reason: Decisions: the meaning of a book title goes in a note at its first occurrence in a unit.

patches.value: ד' is read as the number 4. It may instead abbreviate דף, 'folio'. The reference is kept as the author writes it, not completed or converted.
patches.reason: Decisions: references are given exactly as written, דף → 'folio'. Here ד' י"ב could be 'folio 12' or '4, 12'. Proposed ruling: keep '4, 12' with this note, because the author writes דף in full in the same paragraph (דף מ' ע"א); the owner to confirm.

value: The quotation of Deut 4:4 (4:18.17-23) has no formula; it is set in quotation marks as the author's direct words. The author's own gloss begins with כי (4:18.24) and is not part of the verse.
וכו' (4:18.35, 4:18.71, 4:18.116, 4:18.137) marks an abbreviated passage. It stays as 'etc.' because it marks the truncation.
יה"ו (4:18.56) spells the letters yod, heh, vav of the Name; וה"א אחרונה (4:18.59) is the last heh.
על אדני (4:18.68-69): read as the Name Adonai, in a passage on the divine names and Malkhut. שנעשה שם שלם is 'that a complete name be made'; שם שלם has no article.

אלהא רברבא (4:18.103-104, 108-109) is Aramaic, and occurs twice: as the cited heading after ד"ה, and inside the author's sentence. The verb נקרא has no stated subject, as in ובחכמה נקרא חכם, so 'He is called'. מבואר ('it is explained') introduces indirect speech, so the sentence has no quotation marks.
patches.reason: The notes described the old reading of אדני and of the Aramaic heading.

value: Deut 4:4 (4:18.17-23): 'But you who cleave to the LORD your God are alive, every one of you, today.'
4:18.69: אדני is read as the Name Adonai; the alternative reading is אדני, 'bases' or 'sockets' (plural of אדן).
patches.reason: A real alternative reading of the word is recorded (pilot ruling on ambiguous spellings).
